redFirst.basis: gate-only task with tests.expectRedFirst false and tests.add none: a documentation correction to commands/worktree.md, so no red was owed

outcome.technical: plugins/audit/commands/worktree.md (the only declared file): (1) the remove <phaseId> paragraph now limits --force to the dirty and undescribable refusals; (2) a new paragraph after it states that a tree with a move's copy of the work (or its tombstone) beside it is refused, --force included: exit 1, the refusal names where the copy stands and prints drive-phase.py restore <taskId>, it also refuses when git will not name the tree's git directory, and _worktrees.refuse_unsettled makes the refusal for remove and task-remove alike; (3) remove --path now reads 'the same, refusals included' (the line was rewrapped); (4) task-remove limits --force to its first two refusals and states the forced-or-not refusal naming the copy and the restore command; (5) the exit-1 list adds, for remove and task-remove forced or not, a move's copy beside the tree or a git directory git will not name, with the restore command in the reason. I checked the page against the code: manage-worktrees.py do_remove (the code path for both remove <phaseId> and remove --path) calls _wt.refuse_unsettled at :386, and do_task_remove calls it at :741. Both calls come before the force-gated dirtiness checks and return E_FAIL; E_FAIL is 1 at :112. _worktrees.py refuse_unsettled (:2313) refuses when tree_unsettled answers None (no admin dir) or True, and its remedy is restore_command, i.e. drive-phase.py restore. kept_where (:2256) names the copy's path, its numbered files and its index, which is why the page says 'names where the copy stands' and not 'names the files'. Commands run: none. executor.runsGate is own-tests and the brief says the task adds no test, so it has nothing of its own to run; the orchestrator's recorded run of `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__refs.py tests/test__deps.py tests/test__output_lints.py` is the evidence. Class sweep: `grep -rn 'explicit escape' --include='*.md' .` returned the two hits this change wrote, at worktree.md:56 and :89. `grep -rn task-remove` over the plugin docs, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and docs/research, filtered by force/refuse/dirty, returned README.md:451 (it says remove/task-remove take a tree down and makes no claim that a forced removal succeeds, so I left it) and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:4886 (about status offering task-remove rather than --force for a set-aside key; still correct). Dependants: _worktrees.py:5, manage-worktrees.py:4 and :194 cite worktree.md as the prose that the modules replaced, and the default-path convention; both untouched, still correct. _locks.py:587 and tests/test__refs.py:3606-3682 read the lock section's fenced bash block; untouched, still correct. CHANGELOG.md:2683 is history about branch naming; still correct, and CHANGELOG.md:109-117 now agrees with the page. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:1089 is history; still correct. docs/research/token-efficiency-audit.md:467 lists the page as a component; still correct. Left for the Faults list, outside this resolution: the exit-code line does not list exit 6, which manage-worktrees.py returns as E_SETUP (:116, :682) when task-add's worktreeSetup fails.
outcome.descriptive: /audit:worktree's command page now says, like CHANGELOG and COMPATIBILITY, that remove, remove --path and task-remove refuse a tree with a move's copy beside it, --force included, with exit 1 and the drive-phase.py restore command
